name: VOID//CTF starter pack
description: Six beginner-friendly training challenges. All data is synthetic or fictional; the web target runs only on your machine.

challenges.name: Signal in the Noise
challenges.description:
Our relay intercepted a short transmission. It looks like random noise, but the operator swears it is "just wrapped twice".

```
NjY2YzYxNjc3YjY1Nzg2MTZkNzA2YzY1NWY2YzYxNzk2NTcyNjU2NDVmNjU2ZTYzNmY2NDY5NmU2Nzdk
```

Unwrap it and submit the flag.

hints.title: Padding
hints.content: The outer layer uses an alphabet of 64 characters. What does the decoded text look like next?

hints.title: Second layer
hints.content: Only the characters 0-9 and a-f appear after the first decode. Two of them make one byte.

challenges.name: Ghost in the Metadata
challenges.description:
A frame was exported from a (fictional) harbor CCTV system. The picture shows nothing interesting — but image files carry more than pixels.

Inspect the attachment and recover the operator's note.

hints.title: Tools
hints.content: Try `exiftool`, `strings`, or any PNG chunk viewer.

challenges.name: The Lighthouse Keeper
challenges.description:
A training dossier on a **fictional** person has been prepared for you. Everything you need is inside the attachment — do not search the real internet.

Find the town where Mara Velsk grew up and the year her lighthouse was decommissioned.

Flag format: `flag{example_<town>_<year>}` (lowercase).

hints.title: Dates
hints.content: A birthday post and its date tell you more than the age.

challenges.name: Staff Only
challenges.description:
The (fictional) Saltmere Harbor Authority runs a staff portal. Staff tools are "hidden", and the portal decides who you are in a way that might be a little too trusting.

The target runs **only on your own machine** as part of the training environment — see the connection info below.

hints.title: Where to look
hints.content: Well-behaved crawlers read a certain text file before indexing a site.

hints.title: Who am I?
hints.content: Open your browser's developer tools and look at the cookies this site sets.

challenges.name: Dial Tone
challenges.description:
Someone typed a message on an old phone keypad. Each group of digits is one character, and `0` stands for an underscore.

```
33 99 2 6 7 555 33 0 55 33 999 7 2 3 0 7777 444 4 66 2 555 7777
```

Wrap the decoded text as `flag{...}`.

hints.title: Multi-tap
hints.content: Pressing 2 once is A, twice is B, three times is C.

challenges.name: Deep Signal
challenges.description:
This password checker was recovered from a training workstation. Figure out which password it accepts — that password is the flag.

You can read the script without running it. If you do run it, it only compares a string and prints a result.

*Unlocks after you solve **Signal in the Noise**.*

hints.title: Symmetry
hints.content: XOR-ing twice with the same key gives back the original bytes.
